Tech Stocks Boosted by Cybersecurity Rally
 
Plus, Nvidia slips after earnings and a Fed governor pushes for an aggressive hike
 
By Heard on the Street Staff
 
 
JEENAH MOON/REUTERS
 

This is an edition of the Markets P.M. newsletter, a recap of the day’s most important markets moves, delivered after the closing bell. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

What Happened in Markets Today

 

Tech stocks found their footing after a tough start to the week. The Nasdaq Composite index rose 0.4%, snapping a four-session losing streak. However, the S&P 500 still slid again, by 0.2%, and the Dow Jones Industrial was off by 561 points, or 1.1%.

 

Cybersecurity stocks surged. Okta rose 12%, and Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike were also among the market’s top performers. Investors may be anticipating a wave of spending by corporations on security, following a series of alarming tech outages. Palo Alto Networks reported earnings after the close. It is also acquiring an AI startup, the Journal reported.

 

Robust results didn’t help Nvidia shares. Shares of the chip giant slid almost 3% following its earnings report on Tuesday after close. It reported record sales, higher than Wall Street’s forecast. Interim CEO Colette Kress also said the company was raising its expected revenue growth for fiscal 2028, from 70% to 75%.

 

Health insurance stocks were hammered. Humana and UnitedHealth Group both tumbled by double-digit percentages, leading the S&P 500’s decliners. Analysts pointed to concerns about the impact of Washington policy changes as a catalyst, including a push for expanded Medicare audits.

 

A Fed official called for a potential supersize rate increase. Fed governor Christopher Waller said that a half-point hike in December may be warranted. He said he is “very concerned about inflation” and that “you have to start taking more aggressive actions.” Treasury yields fell, with the 10-year yield dropping to 5.066% from 5.102%.

One Big Story

 
 
MANUEL ORBEGOZO/REUTERS
 

Colette Kress has a daunting job. She also has a tremendous head start.

 

Kress made her first appearance as Nvidia’s interim chief executive on Tuesday at an inflection point for the company. Former CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang is gone. The SEC is investigating whether it misled investors. Questions are swirling about the company’s business with cloud-computing operations in Asia that work with China.

 

But Nvidia is still growing strongly. On Tuesday, Kress signaled confidence by raising her forecast for revenue growth next fiscal year to 75% from 70% previously. Kress’s reset would have been much harder if it happened earlier in the AI boom.

 
 
 

What’s Coming Up

 

• Anthropic shares are anticipated to begin trading on Thursday.

 

• Retailers Walmart, Ross Stores and Gap reports are set to report earnings, as are Alibaba and Intuit.

 

• Economic data will include outlook surveys from the Kansas City Fed and Philadelpha Fed.

 

• Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson and Richmond Fed Thomas Barkin are speaking.
